I therefore tested the narrowing for completeness across every surface that consumed the old claim rather than checking that one field was renamed. shouldFix.appliesTo: CLAUDE-V29-B1 / PTCB-V29-B1 — the subject narrowing is complete; the accompanying demotion of runtimeContinuity is not
shouldFix.title: runtimeContinuity is demoted to HARDENING in two clauses and still described as the interval constraint with absent-indicator refusals in six others, with no precedence rule, so two conforming implementations reach opposite qualification outcomes on the same machine
shouldFix.theTwoDemotedClauses: runtimeContinuity.role now reads 'HARDENING only. Not an interval proof and not sufficient to claim running-kernel-package. Absence does not by itself refuse if the firmware-launched subject and transcript match. Presence may still refuse a machine (fail closed on contradictory values: kexec_loaded=1).' Consistently with that, refusesBootConfigs and unavailableRefuses were both rewritten this generation and neither lists a runtimeContinuity failure or any kexec state among its refusal conditions.
shouldFix.theSixUnreconciledClauses: Inside the same runtimeContinuity object, the indicator sentences still carry the v29 refusals: lockdown says 'Absent file, none, or confidentiality-only without integrity selected refuses'; kexecLoadDisabled says '0 or absent refuses'; kexecLoaded says 'Absent file is success only when kexecLoadDisabled is 1'. enforcedBootPolicy.runtimeContinuity still reads 'This is the post-boot interval constraint. Unavailable indicators refuse this machine.' And whatThisDoesNotDo still carries two v29 lines: 'runtimeContinuity is the interval constraint' and 'Does not leave kexec-enabled machines in scope.' No clause anywhere states which reading governs; the contract contains no precedence sentence for this field, though it has written one twice before for exactly this situation.
shouldFix.failureScenario: Take a machine whose kernel is built without any kernel-replacement support — the strongest configuration for this purpose, and the one I identified at v29 as being penalised by the old indicator set. It exposes neither /proc/sys/kernel/kexec_load_disabled nor /proc/sys/kernel/kexec_loaded. Its firmware-launched subject and signed transcript match perfectly. Implementation A follows kexecLoadDisabled ('0 or absent refuses') and enforcedBootPolicy ('Unavailable indicators refuse this machine') and REFUSES the machine. Implementation B follows role ('Absence does not by itself refuse if the firmware-launched subject and transcript match') and the rewritten refusesBootConfigs and unavailableRefuses, neither of which lists the condition, and QUALIFIES it. Both implementations conform to the text as written. A second divergence follows from the same split: whatThisDoesNotDo asserts kexec-enabled machines are not in scope, while role admits them so long as kexec_loaded is 0 — and refusesBootConfigs, which listed 'kexec enabled or loaded' at v29, no longer does.
shouldFix.whyNotABlocker: Under either reading the attested subject is firmware-launched-kernel-package, which is correctly narrowed and correctly disclosed, so no reading produces a false attestation. The divergence is over which machines qualify, and the stricter branch merely over-refuses. This is a conformance-determinacy defect, not an authenticity hole, and it does not reopen CLAUDE-V29-B1.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Finish the demotion in the clauses that were left behind, and add the precedence sentence this contract already uses elsewhere. Concretely: rewrite the four indicator sentences so that an absent indicator is not a refusal and only a contradictory present value is (matching role); replace enforcedBootPolicy.runtimeContinuity's 'This is the post-boot interval constraint. Unavailable indicators refuse this machine' with the HARDENING characterisation; delete or restate the two stale whatThisDoesNotDo lines so that neither calls runtimeContinuity the interval constraint nor claims kexec-enabled machines are out of scope; and add one governing sentence in the form already used at authenticatedManifest.uniqueness and peCoffImageDigestAlgorithm.specificationGoverns naming role as controlling for this field. Keep the indicators themselves — as hardening they are worth retaining.

repairsVerified.finding: CLAUDE-V29-B1 / PTCB-V29-B1 (mine and Codex's, converged) — present-state indicators do not prove no prior kernel replacement
repairsVerified.result: REPAIRED by the narrowing route, and completely on the subject side. subjectByScheme.package-db.kind is now 'exactly firmware-launched-kernel-package', its digest is 'of the firmware-launched kernel package bytes', canonicalSerialization pins the exact token, and binding requires it. The observation field states the limit in the contract's own words: 'The subject is the firmware-launched kernel package for this boot, not a claim that the currently executing image was never replaced after that launch', and adds that 'present-state kexec sysctls are not this observation'. I asked at v29 that the limitation be recorded where NT-TCB-1 and g22.testMatrix can see it, and it is, at both: a new NT-TCB-DISCLOSE-KEXEC entry records that 'A later kexec of a different signed kernel is outside this bind. Do not treat that gap as NT-TCB-1 inapplicability or as a Linux slice-1 withdrawal', and g22.doesNotClaim now states the same limitation is 'in-scope-disclosure, not a skipped NT-TCB cell'. inScopeBootConfigs, unavailableRefuses and whatThisDoesNotDo each carry the disclosure. I checked every residual mention: 'running-kernel-package' survives only in the demotion sentence, a reviewGuidance attack line, and the honestyRepairs record, and 'running kernel' survives only in the macOS SecCode clauses, which are a different and valid mechanism. Linux stays in platforms.slice1 and no deferral is minted.

repairsVerified.finding: PTCB-V29-B2 — the signed allowlist stopped at kernelEvent and permitted later firmware code before the separator
repairsVerified.result: REPAIRED. measuredBootTranscript.covers is 'every PCR-0/1/2/4 event from the start of the log through the first PCR-4 EV_SEPARATOR inclusive', which is the control-transfer boundary Codex named rather than kernelEvent. measuredBootTranscriptMatch requires field-for-field equality in order — 'same count, same pcrIndex, same pcrSequenceIndex, same eventType, same digestSha256. Extra, missing, type-mismatch, or digest-mismatch refuses' — so no additional code-bearing event can appear after the kernel and before the separator without failing the match. codeJoin requires every codeBearing transcript row except the kernel row to join its digest to a four-field signedEntry.

repairsVerified.finding: PTCB-V29-B3 — the code-versus-config exemption trusted an eventType the quote does not authenticate
repairsVerified.result: REPAIRED, and this is the strongest idea in the generation. The transcript is signed and becomes the authority for type: 'The untrusted log eventType is not used to classify or exempt a row until it equals the transcript eventType at that pcrSequenceIndex', and configRows are 'exempt from signedEntry only when the transcript, not the raw log, names that type at that position'. eventPreimage.rule carries the same discipline into digest recomputation, requiring the grammar-selecting eventType to be 'the measuredBootTranscript eventType at that pcrSequenceIndex, not an unauthenticated log label'. Type, PCR, order and digest are all bound through the signed transcript, which is exactly what Codex required.

repairsVerified.finding: PTCB-V29-S1 — preimage and digest were the same value, yielding incompatible hash equations
repairsVerified.result: REPAIRED. A new recomputeDigest object separates preimageBytes from the digest function for six type families, each applying its function exactly once: PE image types use 'peCoffImageDigestAlgorithm(preimageBytes) once. That output is already SHA-256', and blob, action, variable, separator and version/handoff types use 'SHA-256(preimageBytes) once'. The chain equality Codex specified is stated: the result 'MUST equal event.digests[TPM_ALG_SHA256] and, when a preKernelReferences row exists, that row.recomputedDigest. No second SHA-256 is applied to a value that is already a digest.' EV_NO_ACTION is given 'no preimageBytes; no recomputeDigest; no PCR extend'.

repairsVerified.finding: PTCB-V29-S2 — RPM procedures consumed snapFd after the snapshot transition closed it
repairsVerified.result: REPAIRED. preferredApi now opens by fdopen on roFd, holds roFd across headerBind, digest, verify and extract, states 'Do not close and reopen roFd. The only permitted close/reopen is the snapshot O_RDONLY transition already completed', and adds 'Use of snapFd after close refuses'. snapFd is confined to the creation, sealing and reopen transition.

repairsVerified.finding: PTCB-V29-S3 — EV_NO_ACTION declared non-extending while replay extended every row
repairsVerified.result: REPAIRED. replayAlgorithm.step now filters on type — 'whose eventType is not EV_NO_ACTION' — and states 'EV_NO_ACTION rows are retained in the log and in the transcript but MUST NOT extend.' A dedicated evNoActionVector is reserved as G22 evidence proving the reconstructed PCR is unchanged by such a row, which is the replay vector Codex asked for.

summary: REJECT at 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX. Custody is clean and the one irregularity is disclosed rather than hidden: subject unmoved at 9be8deeb... and 0444 at both ends, HEAD steady, 41/41 chain pins reproduce, 61 changed paths with zero off-roster, reviewGuidance a pure append, Linux still in D-002 slice 1, all 25 D-096 mentions refusals. The frozen Codex v29 verdict was rewritten after reaching COMPLETE, and the subject records that itself, naming the superseded digest and byte count and restating that predecessor-review replacement is not PASS-NO-SCOPE-EFFECT; I record it and do not charge it, noting that the superseded content is unrecoverable here. Every predecessor finding is repaired. The signed measuredBootTranscript is the strongest idea in the sequence: it covers every PCR-0/1/2/4 event through the first PCR-4 separator inclusive with ordered field-for-field equality, and it makes the signed transcript rather than the raw log the authority for event type, so the classification exemption Codex attacked no longer rests on an unauthenticated label. recomputeDigest separates preimageBytes from the digest function for six type families and applies each exactly once, with the full chain equality stated; the RPM stages are confined to roFd with use-after-close refusing; and replay now skips EV_NO_ACTION with a reserved proof vector. My own blocker is closed by the narrowing route: the subject kind is firmware-launched-kernel-package, the observation states plainly that this is 'not a claim that the currently executing image was never replaced after that launch', and the limitation is recorded at both places I asked for — a new NT-TCB-DISCLOSE-KEXEC entry that forbids treating the gap as NT-TCB-1 inapplicability or a Linux withdrawal, and g22.doesNotClaim. What remains is that the demotion accompanying that narrowing was applied unevenly. runtimeContinuity.role now calls it 'HARDENING only. Not an interval proof', and says absence does not by itself refuse; refusesBootConfigs and unavailableRefuses were rewritten to match. But the four indicator sentences inside the same object still say absence refuses, enforcedBootPolicy still calls it 'the post-boot interval constraint' whose 'Unavailable indicators refuse this machine', and whatThisDoesNotDo still carries 'runtimeContinuity is the interval constraint' and 'Does not leave kexec-enabled machines in scope'. No precedence sentence exists, though this contract has written one twice before for exactly this situation. A machine built without kernel-replacement support and matching the transcript refuses under one branch and qualifies under the other, and both implementations conform. That is a determinacy defect rather than an authenticity hole, which is why it is a SHOULD-FIX; finishing the demotion in six clauses and adding one governing sentence closes it.
